- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in the last few days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 5–7 days.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “mean reversion” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% of the spike magnitude from subsequent days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 10+ days, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 7–10 days.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price direction; adjust forecast by adding 0.5–1.0% to the last 3–5 days of history to align with true trend.
